modelGroup: 3D Model of the Structures of the Brain - Left Sagittal View
source: User-provided Head.jpg and 26-term vocabulary list, with a screenshot of the corresponding diagram hotspots. Original photograph retained byte-for-byte. Each prompt specifies the target using printed model labels or anatomical location; no synthetic arrows or altered anatomy.

questions.question: Which cerebral lobe occupies the upper posterior part of the hemisphere, behind the frontal lobe?
questions.typedQuestion: Which cerebral lobe occupies the upper posterior part of the hemisphere, behind the frontal lobe?
questions.explanation: Integrates somatic sensation and spatial information.

questions.question: Which cerebral lobe lies at the anterior end of this model, immediately behind the forehead?
questions.typedQuestion: Which cerebral lobe lies at the anterior end of this model, immediately behind the forehead?
questions.explanation: Supports voluntary motor control, planning, and executive functions.

questions.question: Identify the thick, pale C-shaped band marked 4 in the center of the hemisphere.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the thick, pale C-shaped band marked 4 in the center of the hemisphere.
questions.explanation: This large commissural white-matter tract connects the cerebral hemispheres.

questions.question: Identify the thin partition marked 5, between the corpus callosum above and the fornix below.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the thin partition marked 5, between the corpus callosum above and the fornix below.
questions.explanation: The septum pellucidum separates portions of the lateral ventricles.

questions.question: Identify the curved strip of cerebral cortex immediately superior to and following the arch of the corpus callosum.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the curved strip of cerebral cortex immediately superior to and following the arch of the corpus callosum.
questions.explanation: This medial cortical gyrus forms part of the limbic system.

questions.question: Identify the small commissural white-matter bundle in the anterior wall of the third ventricle, near the anterior column of the fornix.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the small commissural white-matter bundle in the anterior wall of the third ventricle, near the anterior column of the fornix.
questions.explanation: The anterior commissure connects regions of the two cerebral hemispheres.

questions.question: Identify the optic-pathway crossing at the base of the brain, anterior to the pituitary stalk (near label 15).
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the optic-pathway crossing at the base of the brain, anterior to the pituitary stalk (near label 15).
questions.explanation: Some optic nerve fibers cross here before continuing in the optic tracts.

questions.question: Identify the rounded gland marked 16, hanging beneath the hypothalamus in the sella turcica.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the rounded gland marked 16, hanging beneath the hypothalamus in the sella turcica.
questions.explanation: The pituitary is an endocrine gland connected to the hypothalamus by the infundibulum.

questions.question: Identify the small rounded projection on the inferior surface of the hypothalamus, just posterior to the pituitary stalk.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the small rounded projection on the inferior surface of the hypothalamus, just posterior to the pituitary stalk.
questions.explanation: Mammillary bodies participate in limbic memory pathways.

questions.question: Identify the region inferior to the thalamus and superior to the pituitary stalk, forming the floor of the third ventricle.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the region inferior to the thalamus and superior to the pituitary stalk, forming the floor of the third ventricle.
questions.explanation: Coordinates homeostasis, autonomic regulation, and endocrine control.

questions.question: Identify the prominent rounded bulge of the brainstem marked 20, anterior to the cerebellum.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the prominent rounded bulge of the brainstem marked 20, anterior to the cerebellum.
questions.explanation: The pons lies between the midbrain and medulla oblongata.

questions.question: Identify the superior brainstem segment between the diencephalon and pons (the region labeled III).
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the superior brainstem segment between the diencephalon and pons (the region labeled III).
questions.explanation: Contains the cerebral aqueduct and the superior and inferior colliculi.

questions.question: Identify the tapering brainstem segment marked 21, inferior to the pons and continuous with the spinal cord.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the tapering brainstem segment marked 21, inferior to the pons and continuous with the spinal cord.
questions.explanation: Contains important autonomic centers for cardiovascular and respiratory regulation.

questions.question: Identify the long nervous-system structure marked 22 within the vertebral canal, continuing inferiorly from the medulla.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the long nervous-system structure marked 22 within the vertebral canal, continuing inferiorly from the medulla.
questions.explanation: Conducts information between the brain and body and supports spinal reflexes.

questions.question: Identify the large, folded posterior-inferior brain structure behind the pons and medulla.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the large, folded posterior-inferior brain structure behind the pons and medulla.
questions.explanation: Coordinates movement, balance, and motor learning.

questions.question: Identify the branching, tree-like white matter visible within the sectioned cerebellum.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the branching, tree-like white matter visible within the sectioned cerebellum.
questions.explanation: The arbor vitae is cerebellar white matter surrounded by cerebellar cortex.

questions.question: Identify the ventricular space between the pons and upper medulla anteriorly and the cerebellum posteriorly.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the ventricular space between the pons and upper medulla anteriorly and the cerebellum posteriorly.
questions.explanation: This cerebrospinal-fluid cavity connects with the cerebral aqueduct superiorly.

questions.question: Identify the narrow cerebrospinal-fluid passage through the midbrain that connects the third and fourth ventricles.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the narrow cerebrospinal-fluid passage through the midbrain that connects the third and fourth ventricles.
questions.explanation: The cerebral aqueduct passes through the midbrain rather than the pons.

questions.question: Which cerebral lobe occupies the posterior tip of the hemisphere, above the cerebellum at the back of this model?
questions.typedQuestion: Which cerebral lobe occupies the posterior tip of the hemisphere, above the cerebellum at the back of this model?
questions.explanation: The occipital lobe contains the primary visual cortex.

questions.question: Identify the lower of the two dorsal midbrain elevations, inferior to the superior colliculus; it participates in auditory processing.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the lower of the two dorsal midbrain elevations, inferior to the superior colliculus; it participates in auditory processing.
questions.explanation: The inferior colliculi are paired auditory relay structures in the midbrain tectum.

questions.question: Identify the upper dorsal midbrain elevation, below the pineal region and superior to the inferior colliculus; it helps orient the eyes and head toward visual stimuli.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the upper dorsal midbrain elevation, below the pineal region and superior to the inferior colliculus; it helps orient the eyes and head toward visual stimuli.
questions.explanation: The superior colliculi participate in visual orienting responses.

questions.question: Identify the small posterior projection from the roof of the diencephalon, behind the thalamus and above the superior colliculus.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the small posterior projection from the roof of the diencephalon, behind the thalamus and above the superior colliculus.
questions.explanation: The pineal gland is part of the epithalamus and secretes melatonin.

questions.question: Identify the central diencephalic gray-matter mass surrounding the intermediate mass and superior to the hypothalamus.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the central diencephalic gray-matter mass surrounding the intermediate mass and superior to the hypothalamus.
questions.explanation: The thalamus relays most sensory information to the cerebral cortex.

questions.question: Identify the small round central bridge marked 8 within the thalamic region.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the small round central bridge marked 8 within the thalamic region.
questions.explanation: The intermediate mass is the interthalamic adhesion, connecting the medial surfaces of the thalami in many brains.

questions.question: Identify the vascular red-purple strip along the ventricular region above the thalamus, associated with cerebrospinal-fluid production.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the vascular red-purple strip along the ventricular region above the thalamus, associated with cerebrospinal-fluid production.
questions.explanation: Choroid plexuses contain specialized epithelium that produces most cerebrospinal fluid.

questions.question: Identify the slender pale arch marked 6, inferior to the septum pellucidum and corpus callosum.
questions.typedQuestion: Identify the slender pale arch marked 6, inferior to the septum pellucidum and corpus callosum.
questions.explanation: The fornix is a major limbic white-matter pathway associated with the hippocampus.
